newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO's Arafat promises to fight corruption.
newsitem.headline: PLO's Arafat promises to fight corruption.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat admitted on Tuesday some of his cabinet members had squandered public funds and vowed reforms to end corruption, a senior PLO official said.

"We have the courage to admit there are mistakes and have the courage to make reforms and punish violaters, and I inform you officially that the Palestinian Authority will put an end to corruption and squandering of public funds," said Tayeb Abdel-Rahim, general secretary of the Palestinian Authority, reading a letter from Arafat to lawmakers.
"The Palestinian Authority is going to punish any violator regardless of his position if he has harmed our people's interests," he said.

"But at the same time we will not allow anyone to kill the embryonic dream, to kill our Palestinian Authority, our last step towards our independent state," Abdel-Rahim added, referring to some lawmakers who strongly cricitised Arafat and his Authority last week.

Arafat's letter was issued in response to accusations of corruption by lawmakers citing a 600-page report prepared by Arafat's auditing office that concluded some ministers had squandered around $326 million in public funds last year.
Officials said the report named five ministers allegedly involved in the corruption.
Abdel-Rahim said Arafat set up a committe to examine the findings of the report which he handed to the Speaker of the Palestinian Legislative Council for distribution to lawmakers.
"We highly appreciate President Arafat's efforts to publish the report and we are all eager for a system where transparency and the sovereignty of law prevails," Council Speaker Ahmed Korei said.
